comment_box:
The Hyde amendment already ensures that federal funds are not used on elective abortions, only in cases of rape, incest, and where the life of the pregnant person is endangered. The main effect of this policy thus seems to be to deny options to rape and incest survivors. I strongly oppose this change.

The exception for treatment "when a physician certifies that the life of the mother would be endangered if the fetus were carried to term" also seems very narrow; for example, it would not apply to cases where the fetus is certainly non-viable and will not survive after birth, but continuing the pregnancy to term would be likely to result in the mother's permanent physical disability. If this is not intended, the rule should be expanded to also cover the risk of permanent physical injury/disability. If it is intended, respectfully, I think it shocks the conscience to tell a rape survivor that she must carry to term, even if there is no chance of a living child and she will be permanently disabled as a result. Veterans deserve better.
